proposals.before: At the beginning of Yong'an in Wei, his second elder brother Hui was betrothed to Liang; he memorialized that Xi be released from commoner status and made attendant cavalier, and Xi was summoned to serve as recorder on the staff of Prince of Guangping's opening office.
proposals.after: At the beginning of Yong'an in Wei, his second elder brother Hui went on mission to Liang; he memorialized that Xi be released from commoner status and made attendant cavalier, and Xi was summoned to serve as recorder on the staff of Prince of Guangping's opening office.
proposals.reason: 聘梁 means a diplomatic mission/envoy posting to Liang, not betrothal.

proposals.before: When the prince reached Ye, Yang Yin, Murong Yan and others were executed; an edict made him grand chancellor, commander-in-chief of all armies within and without, overseeing civil and military affairs; he returned to Bing.
proposals.after: When the prince reached Ye, Yang, Yan and others were executed; an edict made him grand chancellor, commander-in-chief of all armies within and without, overseeing civil and military affairs; he returned to Bing.
proposals.reason: Chinese has 楊、燕 without Murong; idiomatic invents the surname Murong.

proposals.before: Xi had his wife answer; the wife never spoke; Xi pat his chest with his hand and withdrew.
proposals.after: Xi had his wife answer; the wife never spoke; Xi patted his chest with his hand and withdrew.
proposals.reason: English verb form error: "pat" should be "patted".

decisions.reason: In s0059, 第二兄暉聘梁 is an envoy posting to Liang, not a betrothal; 'was betrothed to Liang' misreads 聘 and invents a marriage alliance with a state.
Chinese has only 誅楊、燕等; 'Murong Yan' invents a surname absent from the unit, and reducing to 'Yang, Yan and others' matches the source abbreviations.
Narrative past tense requires 'patted' for 拊胸; the literal's 'pat' is an English verb-form error, and the proposed fix matches the Chinese action.
